pending_items.title: Israel kills Gaza deputy education minister and wife in fresh attack on Gaza
pending_items.content:
A senior Palestinian education official and his wife have become the latest victims of a string of Israeli attacks targeting Hamas officials this week, medical sources report.

Khaled Abu Nada, undersecretary of Gaza's Ministry of Education, and his wife were killed in an Israeli attack on a residential block in central Gaza's Deir el-Balah, according to medics at Al-Aqsa Hospital. They added that another six people were wounded, some of them critically.

Abu Nada was a member of Hamas's political bureau, and also served as deputy education minister.

Al Jazeera reported that Israeli Apache helicopters "without warning" fired "two missiles directly and in succession" at Abu Nada's apartment, adding that the attack took place during dawn prayers, and that the surrounding area was crowded with tents where displaced families were sheltering.

Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz confirmed Abu Nada's killing, claiming that he was “a Hamas figure responsible for the group’s economy and education portfolios”.

They added that his death forms part of a "targeted operation” waged against “operatives and senior officials” belonging to Hamas, claiming that they had killed around 80 of the group’s members in the last month.

The Israeli officials did not make any suggestion of Abu Nada having a military role in Hamas.

Abu Nada’s assassination follows a string of other attacks on Hamas officials in recent days.

Early on Wednesday, Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, internal security chief for northern Gaza, was killed alongside his wife and two daughters, aged 13 and 15. Naim Abu Nahl, Gaza’s internal security director, was killed the day before.

Gaza's Ministry of Interior said that the assassinations are an attempt by Israel to sow chaos in the territory.

“What stands out is the direct targeting by Israeli forces through the assassination of security and police commanders," the ministry's spokesperson, Abu Amra said.

The Jerusalem Post reported that Abu Nada’s killing marks a “turning point in Israel’s targeted assassination policy in Gaza” with the aim of collapsing Hamas’s "control over the enclave”.

Hamas condemned Abu Nada’s killing as “a new crime added to the occupation's long record of targeting civilians, educational personnel, residential apartments and neighbourhoods in the Strip".

Meanwhile, Israeli attacks killed another seven Palestinians on Thursday.

Wafa news agency reported that at least three people were killed and others wounded when Israeli forces fired a drone at a group of people in northern Gaza’s al-Shati camp, west of Gaza City.

According to Al Jazeera, Israeli forces shot dead a 62-year-old man in Bureij refugee camp, in central Gaza.

A Gaza health ministry spokesperson described the surge in attacks in recent months as “a systematic targeting of all the pillars of life in the Gaza Strip”.

Hamas chief Khalil Al-Hayya - who narrowly escaped assassination himself - said on Thursday that the group was not prepared to withstand continued Israeli ​attacks.

He said the movement would discuss with other Palestinian factions how to respond to "Israeli violations and the policy of daily killing”.

"The equation of killing and blockade cannot be accepted under the (ceasefire) agreement," he added.

Gaza’s health ministry reported that Israel has killed at least 1,600 Palestinians, including 130 this month, since the so-called “ceasefire” was imposed last October.

It added that at least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks since October 2023.

UN human rights chief Volker Turk warned on Wednesday of a growing risk of further atrocity crimes against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank , urging all states to take immediate action to prevent them.

Turk cited inflammatory statements by senior Israeli officials advocating annexation, ethnic cleansing and collective punishment, alongside increasingly widespread and systematic violations against Palestinians.

“Across society, the incitement to hatred and to perpetration of violations amounting to atrocity crimes - war crimes, crimes against humanity and even genocide - has been appalling,” he said in a statement.

pending_items.title: Israeli group promoting illegal settlements touring UK reported to police over 'threat'
pending_items.content:
An Israeli non-profit organisation promoting illegal settlements in occupied Palestinian territory that is touring Britain has been reported to the police over an alleged threat to the Palestinian rector of Glasgow University, Dr Ghassan Abu-Sittah.

Abu-Sittah, a British Palestinian surgeon who operated in Gaza during Israel's genocide and is the rector of Glasgow University, had last week criticised Shivat Zion and the "failure of the British government to move against these companies, that are basically facilitating the commission of crimes".

In a statement to the National newspaper earlier this week Shraga Evers, a senior Shivat Zion official, responded by saying: "Honestly, I don’t care what Sheikh Ghassan Abu-Sittah says; he is a Hamas supporter - it’s like asking me about a statement by a staunch Adolf Hitler fan about Jews.

"I would like to send him our regards in his own language: كُلّ كَلْب بِيجِي يُومُه [every dog has its day]. Nazi and Hamas ideology isn’t distant from each other with regards to Jews."

The Arabic phrase "every dog has its day" was used by Israeli officials in relation to Yahya Sinwar, the Hamas leader in Gaza whom Israel killed in 2024. Shivat Zion works with the Israeli Ministry of Aliyah and Integration, and says on its website : "We’re here to help with your Aliyah and Integration into Israeli life!"

Last week MEE reported that a page on Shivat Zion's website promotes a kibbutz in Gush Etzion, a collection of settlements in the illegally occupied West Bank, while other pages promoted events and teacher training in illegal Israeli settlements.

Shivat Zion's two-week tour began last Sunday with an event in Glasgow and is continuing in cities across Britain.

MEE has approached Shivat Zion for comment.

Abu-Sittah responded by calling Evers' remarks "incitement to violence", adding: "If this was a country with a functioning police force, that didn't spend its time arresting thousands of pensioners because they held up a placard, then this man would be arrested."

Evers has said he lives in Efrat, an illegal West Bank settlement. He is currently touring the UK with Shivat Zion.

MEE understands that Jewish Anti-Zionist Action (Jaza), a British activist group, has reported Shivat Zion and Evers to Police Scotland.

Talia Woodin, a spokesperson for Jaza, said: "Shivat Zion is so confident sending a racist, violent diatribe to a newspaper because of the impunity it feels, bolstered by the Israeli state’s support for pro-settlement groups."

Woodin added: "Making a death threat against a heroic British Palestinian doctor and elected university official is utterly deplorable and must now be the last straw. This extremist group must be sanctioned and banned from operating in the UK."

Labour MP Abtisam Mohamed asked Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband "what specific action can be taken against" Shivat Zion during a parliamentary Foreign Affairs Committee hearing earlier this week.

Miliband said he would not comment on Shivat Zion specifically, but added: "We do not want to see advertising of settlement property. We do not want to see advertising of those sorts of opportunities."

Pressed on whether action would be taken against Shivat Zion, he responded: "We will ensure we have a comprehensive [sanctions] regime."

In September, the UK government recognised Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory as illegal and announced comprehensive sanctions on Israeli settlements.

Implementing the full sanctions could take up to nine months, according to government sources.

Sara Husseini, the director of the British Palestinian Committee, said Shivat Zion spokesperson Evers "has exposed the prejudice and disdain in which they hold Palestinians, underscoring the intent to ethnically cleanse the Palestinian people from our homeland with the full backing and involvement of the Israeli state".

Husseini added: "The UK, particularly in light of its recent announcements on sanctions, should take swift action to ban such organisations from promoting unlawful activities."

MEE has contacted Police Scotland for comment.

pending_items.title: Risks of child marriage in Iran complicated by war
pending_items.content:
For a girl still at school, marriage can mean leaving her education behind, becoming pregnant before adulthood and growing dependent on her family and husband.

In Iran, rights advocates warn that war and mounting financial hardship could expose more girls to those risks.

The warning comes as the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage is observed on November 27. The day was established during the UN General Assembly last year.

Although there is no evidence linking child marriages to the war, cases illustrate the danger faced by girls married as children, often with limited means of escaping abuse. Gaps in Iran's marriage statistics also make it difficult to measure the conflict's impact.

In one case cited by the Iranian human rights news agency HRANA, a 14-year-old girl in Kerman province who had recently given birth was reportedly killed by her husband .

Skylar Thompson, deputy director of Human Rights Activists in Iran (HRA), said she had reportedly been forced to marry at 13.

"While these cases cannot be directly attributed to the war, there are substantial grounds for concern that deteriorating socioeconomic conditions are placing more girls at risk ," Thompson told DW.

Iran Open Data's analysis of the Civil Registration Organization's statistical yearbook identified 14,039 registered marriages involving girls under 15 in year measured roughly from March 2025 to March 2026. They accounted for just over 3% of all registered marriages.

The figure excludes girls aged 15 to 17. UNICEF defines child marriage as a formal marriage or informal union involving someone under 18.

Thompson said 31,646 marriages involving girls under 15 were registered in 2020–2021, indicating a longer-term decline in recorded cases.

But the latest figures largely predate the war , which began on February 28, 2026.

"The absence of recent, disaggregated statistics, coupled with the prevalence of unregistered marriages, makes it difficult to determine whether child marriage has increased since the outbreak of the war," she said.

The conflict has intensified pressures that can contribute to child marriage: lost income, difficulty staying in school and girls' financial dependence on their families.

In its October assessment, the World Bank described damage to infrastructure, disrupted trade and declining purchasing power, forecasting a 7.7% economic contraction in 2026/27.

Thompson told DW that families facing severe hardship may see marriage as a way to reduce household expenses, transfer financial responsibility or secure their daughters' future. Government backed marriage loans can also create financial incentives for some disadvantaged families to arrange marriages involving minors, she added.

Hossein Raeesi, a lawyer and adjunct professor in Carleton University's Department of Law and Legal Studies in Canada, described a similar risk.

When families cannot meet a girl's living costs, and education or other prospects are unavailable, they may push her towards marriage or force her into it, he told DW, while acknowledging that statistics on changes in numbers of child marriages since the war are still unavailable.

Displacement can further weaken children's access to education and protection. On March 12, the UN refugee agency estimated that up to 3.2 million people had been temporarily displaced within Iran, based on preliminary assessments. That was an early-war estimate, rather than a current displacement figure.

Thompson said displacement and disrupted schooling could isolate girls from teachers, social workers and others who might recognize pressure to marry and intervene

Financial dependence, limited independent legal assistance and insufficient shelters can leave girls with few alternatives, particularly when those arranging a marriage are also their legal guardians.

Article 1041 of Iran's Civil Code allows girls under 13 and boys under 15 to marry with guardian consent and court approval. Iranian law therefore provides no blanket prohibition on marriage below 18.

"Although Iranian law formally recognizes consent as a condition of marriage, it provides inadequate practical safeguards against familial coercion," Thompson told DW.

Raeesi said preventing a marriage was insufficient if a girl remained under pressure at home. Leaving home could also expose her to further danger without safe accommodation and practical support.

The concerns also extend to the online space. An HRA investigation published in October reported that the government-licensed matchmaking platform Adam and Eve displayed girls aged 13 to 17 as prospective spouses. Those findings do not establish how many marriages resulted or whether the war increased them.

Raeesi called for a minimum marriage age of 18 for both sexes, alongside preventive intervention, financial assistance, education and safe accommodation.

"Education alone is not enough," he told DW. Families also need the means to support their children.

Thompson urged targeted financial assistance, measures to keep girls in school, confidential reporting channels and independent legal support. Safe accommodation must be accessible without permission from guardians who may themselves be responsible for coercion, she said.

According to rights advocates, effective protection means that a girl under pressure to marry can say no without losing her home, her safety or her chance to continue school.

pending_items.title: US broadcaster airs ad highlighting military aid to Israel during Saturday Night Live
pending_items.content:
A 30-second advert highlighting US taxpayer funding for Israel was broadcast across the United States on Wednesday night during a Thanksgiving special edition of the long-running sketch show Saturday Night Live.

The ad, from the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project (Imeu), a pro- Palestinian advocacy group based in California, shows an American girl carrying out chores over the course of the year in order to make $400 to buy a new bicycle.

The footage then cuts from the American on a pristine suburban street to a Palestinian girl amid the rubble of Gaza. The Palestinian girl has lost a leg to Israeli bombs and is on crutches.

“Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this,” says the ad's American narrator, against the backdrop of the girl in Gaza.

The US currently officially gives Israel $3.8bn a year, in a 10-year memorandum of understanding that runs from 2019 to 2028, working out at just over $360 every three seconds.

The package also includes $3.3bn in foreign military financing and $500m in cooperative missile defence programmes, meaning that the advert's figure is accurate.

At the end of the ad, the viewer is directed to a website called No More For Israel , which tells you that "the US government has sent Israel over $330bn in inflation-adjusted dollars since 1948. That’s $400 every three seconds non-stop for nearly 80 years."

"Right now, behind closed doors, the White House is negotiating a new long-term weapons giveaway to Israel that is estimated to send at least $19bn more of our tax dollars to Israel over the next five years: another $400 every three seconds," the site says.

Israeli newspapers, the country's foreign ministry and pro-Israel figures in the US have hit out at broadcaster NBC for airing the advert.

End Jew Hatred, a group linked to the Lawfare Project, called the advert "antisemitic Hamas propaganda" and circulated a petition demanding that NBC stop broadcasting it.

Jonathan Greenblatt, CEO of the Anti-Defamation League, wrote on X : "Broadcasting an ad that blatantly demonizes the Jewish state and makes false claims about the use of American taxpayer dollars during primetime on the eve of a family holiday isn’t just insensitive. It’s indefensible.

"Again and again, why do people in positions of authority fail to demonstrate basic decency, let alone respect, for the Jewish community? At a moment of escalating antisemitism, there is no rationale to justify fanning the flames with such a twisted narrative."

Greenblatt did not elaborate on what the "twisted narrative" of the advert was or offer any evidence for why its claims were "false".

Self-described "accidental activist" Samantha Ettus said that the advert "promotes the lie that Israel deliberately targets children", more than 20,000 of whom have been killed in Gaza by Israel. "It never mentions Hamas. It never mentions October 7, the hostages, or the rockets Israel is defending against," Ettus posted on X .

Israel’s foreign ministry said: “Don’t let anyone exploit your loved ones’ compassion this holiday season. Ask who’s funding this campaign, whose real goal is the destruction of Israel.”

“We are airing this ad because the American people deserve to know where their money is going,” Margaret DeReus, Imeu's executive director, told Semafor.

Viewing figures for Wednesday's broadcast have yet to be released, but last year's Thanksgiving special attracted approximately 2.7 million viewers.

رییس‌جمهوری آمریکا جمعه ششم آذر در پیامی در شبکه اجتماعی تروث سوشال از اقدامات نخست‌وزیر عراق برای «اعمال اقتدار دولت در سراسر کشور، جلوگیری از قاچاق نفت، مقابله با فساد و قرار دادن همه سلاح‌ها تحت کنترل انحصاری دولت» حمایت کرد.

ترامپ همچنین نوشت از تلاش الزیدی برای ساختن «عراقی متحد، برخوردار از رفاه و قدرتمند» حمایت می‌کند که بتواند تصمیم‌های سیاسی خود را مستقل بگیرد.

حیدر العبودی، سخنگوی دولت عراق، ششم آذر به خبرگزاری رسمی این کشور (واع) گفت بغداد صادرات نفت خارج از سازوکار وزارت نفت و شرکت دولتی بازاریابی نفت عراق، سومو، را قاچاق می‌داند، زیرا درآمد آن به خزانه دولت نمی‌رسد.

او به نقل از دیوان نظارت مالی عراق گفت زیان ناشی از صادرات نفت اقلیم کردستان خارج از این سازوکارها، از دی ۱۳۸۶ تا دی ۱۴۰۴، بیش از ۱۰۰ میلیارد دلار بوده است.

بر اساس گزارش خبرگزاری رویترز، شیوه محاسبه این رقم روشن نیست.
